summary: Thread panel keeps several conversations with an agent in one place, one tab per thread, with a reply field under the open thread. People switch between threads with the tabs and answer the agent without leaving the panel.
use: When one person runs several tasks with the same agent and needs to jump between them.
When a side panel next to the main work should hold the agent conversations.
When each thread has a status you want to show at a glance, like done, waiting or idle.
When agent replies should show the files or pages they drew on.
features: Each thread gets a tab with a coloured dot set by `color`, and an underline slides to the open tab.
The open thread can be controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, or left to the tabs with `defaultValue`.
The reply field submits on Enter and calls `onSend` with the text and the open thread's id. The Send button stays disabled while the field is empty.
A message with `thinking` shows a shimmering "Thinking" line while the agent works, and agent messages can carry `sources` as chips with tooltips.
Switching threads staggers the messages in, and a new message scrolls smoothly into view.
The draft can be controlled with `draft` and `onDraftChange`, and `bare={false}` gives the panel its own card.
a11y: The tabs use `role="tablist"` and `role="tab"` with `aria-selected` on the open thread.
The message area is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so new replies are announced.
The reply field is labelled "Reply" and the icon button is labelled "Send".

faq.q: Does sending a reply add it to the thread automatically?
faq.a: No. `onSend` gives you the text and the thread id, and you add the message to that thread's `messages` to show it. The field clears itself after sending.

faq.q: How do I show that the agent is working on a reply?
faq.a: Add an agent message with `thinking: true`. It shows a shimmering "Thinking", or its `text` if you give one, until you replace it with the real reply.

faq.q: Can I open a specific thread from outside the panel?
faq.a: Yes. Pass the thread's id as `value` and update it from your own state. Use `onValueChange` to hear when someone clicks a tab.
